question: It's been three years since my bachelor's. Will the gap count against me?
expected_location: The applicant’s education history, study and post-study plans
reference_answer: It can be taken into account, but what matters is whether you have sound reasons for returning to study. When assessing your application, caseworkers can consider how long it's been since you last studied and your reasons for coming back to this subject, particularly after a significant gap, along with things like your commitment to the course and how it fits your plans.

question: Can I transfer to a different university after I arrive, or do I need a whole new visa?
expected_location: Students: changing course, without needing permission from the Home Office;The Student or Child Student has not completed the course which their current permission was granted for
reference_answer: No, not on your current visa: you can only change course without a new application if you stay at the university you're already studying at. To move to a different university you need a new Student visa application before you change course.

question: If I fail a module and the resit is after my visa expires, can I extend it?
expected_location: Showing academic progress|ST 14.4|Exemptions
reference_answer: Yes, you can apply to extend. An extension normally requires your new studies to be at a higher academic level than your current course, but resitting exams or repeating modules is one of the exceptions, so you don't need to show academic progress for it.

question: If I drop out halfway through the year, how long can I stay in the UK?

question: I want to start a PhD straight after my master's. Can I apply from inside the UK, or do I have to go home?
expected_location: Extend your visa|The Student or Child Student has completed the course for which they were given permission to stay;Extend your visa > When to apply|ST 4.2|ST 4.3
reference_answer: Yes, you can apply from inside the UK by extending your Student visa, as long as you have an unconditional offer shown on a CAS and the PhD is at a higher academic level than your master's, which it is. You can apply up to 3 months before the PhD starts, but you must apply before your current visa expires and within 6 months of getting your CAS, and the PhD must start within 28 days of your current visa expiring. You can stay in the UK while you wait for the decision.

question: I'm doing a one-year taught master's. Can my wife and our toddler come with me as dependants?
expected_location: Your partner and children|ST 31.1|When student dependants are permitted
reference_answer: No. For postgraduate courses starting on or after 1 January 2024, you can only bring dependants if the course is a PhD or other doctorate or a research-based higher degree, so a one-year taught master's doesn't qualify. The exception is a government-sponsored student on a full-time course of 6 months or longer.

question: My master's dissertation runs over the summer. Does that count as a vacation, so I can work full-time?
reference_answer: I can't find this in the documents I have. Your university's international student advice team can tell you whether your dissertation period counts as an official vacation.

question: Is an unpaid internship OK, or does it count as work?
expected_location: Volunteering
reference_answer: An unpaid internship is allowed, but if it has set duties and obligations it counts as voluntary work, which counts toward your term-time hours limit together with any paid work. Only volunteering (no contract or obligations, not replacing an employee, usually for a charity) doesn't count as work. The guidance doesn't mention internships by name, so this applies the voluntary work rules.

question: Once my course has officially ended but before my visa runs out, can I work full-time?
expected_location: Work conditions
reference_answer: Yes. The guidance says the time left on your visa after you've completed your course counts as outside term time for work purposes, and full-time work is allowed outside term time. The one limit is that you can't take a permanent full-time job unless you've applied for a Graduate or Skilled Worker visa.

question: I finished my master's in September but my results only come out in mid-December. If I apply before 1 January 2027, do I still get two years?
expected_location: Period of grant for a Graduate|How long you can stay|Staying longer in the UK|Extend your visa;When to apply|GR 4.3|Sponsor notification
reference_answer: Yes. A Graduate visa applied for before 1 January 2027 lasts two years (18 months on or after that date), but you can only apply once your university has told the Home Office you've successfully completed your course, so your results need to be reported before then. You don't need to wait for your graduation ceremony, but your Student visa must still be valid on the day you apply.

question: Do I need another English test for the Skilled Worker visa if I already have a UK master's?
expected_location: Academic qualification|EL 3.1
reference_answer: No. A master's degree awarded in the UK meets the English language requirement, and you can prove it with your degree certificate, academic transcript or a letter from your university. You may also meet it if you already showed English at the required level in a previous successful application.

question: Can I fly home for Christmas while my Graduate visa application is pending, and once it's granted, can I travel abroad and come back?
expected_location: Proving your identity and providing supporting documents;What you can and cannot do
reference_answer: No: you must not travel outside the UK, Ireland, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man until you get a decision, or your application will be withdrawn. Once the Graduate visa is granted, you can travel abroad and return to the UK.

question: I've got a graduate job offer and I'm applying for a Skilled Worker visa while I'm still on my Student visa. How early can I start the job?
reference_answer: Once you've made a valid Skilled Worker application, you can start the job up to 3 months before your course completion date. This applies if you're on a full-time course at degree level or above at a higher education provider with a track record of compliance, you applied while you had Student permission, and the application hasn't been decided yet (or an administrative review of a refusal is still pending).

question: My scholarship covers my tuition but not my living costs. Do I still have to show living costs, and what evidence do I need from my sponsor?
expected_location: FIN 8.3|Money to support yourself ('financial requirement')|When student dependants are permitted;FIN 9.1
reference_answer: Yes. You can combine sources, so an official financial sponsor (such as a government, the British Council, an international organisation or company, or a university) can cover your tuition while you show your own money or a student loan for living costs, unless you've been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months. For the scholarship, you need either the funding stated on your CAS, if your university is the sponsor, or a letter of confirmation from the sponsor.

question: My parents' savings are in Indian rupees. Which exchange rate is used to check the amount, and how long does the money need to have been in the account?
expected_location: FIN 1.1;Money to support yourself ('financial requirement')|ST 12.6|Student: financial requirement
reference_answer: The rupees are converted into pounds using the spot exchange rate on www.oanda.com for the date of your application. The money must have been in the account for at least 28 days in a row, and that 28-day period must end within 31 days of the date you apply.

question: My CAS says I need an ATAS certificate. Do I need it before I apply, and how far ahead of my course start can I send in my visa application?
expected_location: ST 8.4|Documents you'll need to apply|ATAS requirements;Applying from outside the UK|ST 4.1|ST 4.2
reference_answer: Yes, you must already have a valid ATAS certificate and include it with your visa application. If you're applying from outside the UK, the earliest you can apply is 6 months before your course starts; from inside the UK, it's 3 months before.

question: I'm starting a PhD in Manchester, and my wife and son are coming with me. How much extra money do I need to show for them, and can my wife work while we're here?
expected_location: Money they need to support themselves|Financial requirement for dependent partner of a Student|Financial requirement for dependent child of a Student|Calculating funds needed for a dependant of a Student;Employment for dependants of a Student|ST 39.3
reference_answer: Because Manchester is outside London, you need £680 a month for each of them for up to 9 months, so £6,120 each and £12,240 in total, on top of the money for your own course and living costs, held for at least 28 consecutive days ending within 31 days of the application. Your wife can work in the UK: the exceptions only cover dependants whose student partner moves on to a new course shorter than 9 months or below degree level, which a PhD isn't.

question: I've been in the UK for 13 months on my Student visa and want to go straight from my master's into a PhD. Can I apply from inside the UK, and do I need to show funds again?
expected_location: Extend your visa|The Student or Child Student has completed the course for which they were given permission to stay;When you do not need to prove you have money to support yourself|ST 12.1
reference_answer: Yes, you can extend your Student visa from inside the UK if you have an unconditional offer on a CAS and the PhD is at a higher academic level than your master's, which it is. Because you've been living in the UK with a visa for at least 12 months before applying, you don't need to prove you have money to support yourself.

question: My master's is only 9 months long. When does my Student visa run out, and does a course that short still count for the Graduate visa?
expected_location: Period and conditions of grant for a Student;How long you studied in the UK for|Study in the UK requirement|Study in the UK requirement
reference_answer: Your Student visa runs until 2 months after your course end date, because that's the extra time given for courses of 6 months or longer but shorter than 12 months. A course that short can still count for the Graduate visa as long as you studied in the UK for its whole length, and you must be in the UK when you apply.

question: Can I do Deliveroo or Uber Eats shifts on a Student visa?
expected_location: What you can and cannot do|ST 26.5|Student and Child Student: Prohibited work;Work Conditions for a Student|Work conditions
reference_answer: It depends on how the work is set up. On a Student visa you can't be self-employed, so you can't do delivery shifts as a self-employed or freelance rider. If the role is a job where the company employs you, it's allowed within your normal work limits: up to 20 hours a week during term time if you're studying at degree level at a university (10 hours if your course is below degree level), and full-time outside term time. The rules don't say whether delivery app riders count as employed or self-employed, so check your contract before you start. If it treats you as self-employed, you can't take the work.

question: I'm finishing my PhD, and my wife is here as my dependant. How long will my Graduate visa last, and can she stay on it with me?
expected_location: How long you can stay|Period of grant for a Graduate|Staying longer in the UK|Extend your visa;Your partner and children|GR 9.4A
reference_answer: With a PhD, your Graduate visa lasts 3 years from the day it's approved. Your wife can apply to stay as your dependant on it because she joined you as a dependant on your current Student visa, and her visa would end on the same date as yours.

question: My government scholarship paid my fees and living costs for my master's. Do I need my government's permission to apply for the Graduate visa, and how much will the application cost?
expected_location: Other documents you might need|GR 1.5;How much it costs|Overview > How much it costs|How much it costs > Healthcare surcharge|Overview > How long you can stay
reference_answer: Yes: if your government paid both your course fees and living costs in the last 12 months, you need a letter from it approving your application. The application fee is £937 plus a healthcare surcharge of usually £1,035 for each year, so it depends on when you apply: on or before 31 December 2026 the visa lasts 2 years (around £2,070 surcharge, £3,007 in total), and on or after 1 January 2027 it lasts 18 months (around £1,552.50 surcharge, £2,489.50 in total).

question: I already had a Graduate visa after my bachelor's here. If I come back for a master's, can I get another one afterwards?
expected_location: GR 1.4|Validity requirements
reference_answer: No. You can't get a Graduate visa if you've been granted one before, or permission under the Doctorate Extension Scheme, so you can't get a second one after your master's.
